items.title: Google Antigravity rolls out Remote Agents for cloud-based agentic coding
facts: Antigravity Remote Agents run your agent sessions and tools in an isolated, Google-managed remote environment rather than on your local machine.

Because execution happens remotely, Remote Agents continue working on long-running tasks and executing commands even when you close your browser, put your laptop to sleep, or switch between desktop and mobile devices.
Available to Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra subscribers signed in with a personal Google Account.

x_posts.author: @vipinxtwt
x_posts.text:
Google Antigravity’s Remote Agents are officially rolling out:

​• Runs inside isolated Google cloud sandboxes (no local machine needed)
• Start in CLI (agy --remote-agent), review on web/phone at http://antigravity.google.com
• Native GitHub repo cloning & Google Drive context
• Permission presets: turbo, default, or per-command approval
• Available on Google AI Pro & Ultra
​Closing your laptop doesn't stop your agent anymore.

x_posts.author: @ArcyDev
x_posts.text:
Google Antigravity Remote Agents — 5 key things:

- Run in isolated, Google-managed cloud environments.
- Keep working even when your computer is off.
- Can access GitHub repositories and Google Drive files.
- Start tasks on desktop and manage them from your phone.
- Available on Google AI Pro and Ultra, with a gradual rollout.

items.title: JetBrains Air ships in 2026.3 IDEs as agentic workbench with free Junie Lite
facts: Air in IDEs is JetBrains’ workspace for coding agents in JetBrains IDEs.
Starting from version 2026.3, the plugin is bundled with JetBrains IDEs.
Junie Lite is free with a JetBrains account.

x_posts.author: @literallydenis
x_posts.text:
we've completely rebuilt how AI agents work inside JetBrains IDEs

it's called Air, and starting with 2026.3 it ships with all our IDEs

Some features:

⛽︎ sign in with your existing ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or Google account. Claude subscriptions work in terminal view

⛽︎ or bring your own OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini API key for supported chat agents

⛽︎ agents work right next to your code, so you can jump into any file they touch without leaving the IDE

⛽︎ hit a limit mid-task? switch to another subscription or API key right in the session, the work keeps going

⛽︎ Claude Agent, Codex, Junie and Copilot work out of the box. add Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenCode, Pi and more from the ACP registry, or connect your own agent through ACP

⛽︎ run agents in parallel in separate Git worktrees, then cherry-pick their changes back

⛽︎ agents get the IDE's symbol search, rename refactoring, inspections and run configurations, plus the debugger in IntelliJ IDEA and CLion

⛽︎ Junie Lite is free with a JetBrains account

⛽︎ leave notes on code or diffs and send them to your agent, Claude Code and Codex terminal sessions included

⛽︎ set up MCP servers once for every new agent chat, add skills from folders or GitHub

⛽︎ see at a glance which agents are running and which are waiting for you, use Caps Lock is LED of agents status

⛽︎ review the last turn, roll back individual files

⛽︎ stuck in a merge conflict? hand it to an agent right from the merge dialog

⛽︎ save agent presets and pin the prompts you keep reusing

⛽︎ macOS, Windows, Linux. Remote Development over SSH, WSL and dev containers too

and yes, you can change the chat text size

and much more features are coming before NY

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.319 adds background MCP tasks and permission controls
facts: Added support for MCP tasks in the terminal: when an MCP server runs a tool call as a task, Claude Code moves it to the background right away and tells Claude the result when it finishes.
Added permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting setting: a tool call that would wait on a permission prompt is denied and the turn continues, in terminal sessions, subagents and teammates.
Fixed a sandbox escape when creating a worktree.

x_posts.author: @alexmichael
x_posts.text:
Claude Code 2.1.319 just dropped, here's what matters

> MCP tool calls that run as tasks now move to the background and report back when done
 > New /claude-api latency-optimize finds where your API code makes people wait
 > Finished subagents stay in /tasks so you can reopen and message them later
 > New denyInsteadOfPrompting setting denies a call instead of stalling on a permission prompt
 > Gateway admins get warnings ahead of Claude Desktop's Nov 10 change
 > Security: fixed a worktree sandbox escape and two ways around permission checks (Bash env prefix, sed)

x_posts.author: @sunset_evm

items.title: OpenAI recaps Agents API updates including auto review and automations
facts: You can now update the tools in an existing session in the Agents API public beta.
Added automatic review for eligible Agents API projects.
Added scheduled automations to the Agents API public beta.

x_posts.author: @AzianMike
x_posts.text:
We shipped a bunch of stuff in Agents API in October! 
And make sure you read to the end for some beta features 👀

The full list:
  - auto review: automatically review and approve or deny supported agent actions, similar to Codex’s “review for me” 
  - automations: you or the agent can schedule future work, including recurring tasks. things like "check on x every hour" automatically work 
  - update tools mid-session: change the tools available to an agent while a session is running 
  - Artifact SDK: hosted sandboxes will now be better at spreadsheets, presentations and Word documents 
  - (experimental) time awareness: experimental setting that gives the agent an understanding of time, so things like "do x in <10 mins" work well 
  - sandbox prewarming: you can prewarm sandboxes before you need them (speeds things up by doing expensive work like installing packages) 
  - async compaction: on by default, compacts context in the background so it doesn’t block the agent 
  - cross-session prompt caching: system prompts are automatically cached across sessions 
  - GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast: use ultrafast mode in the Agents API for faster output 
  - sandbox snapshots: hosted environments can be restored after going idle, with their files intact 
  - 12hr prompt caching: makes things faster for cases where your users talk to the agent less frequently
  - environment keys: create environment keys programmatically 
  - turn-level history: inspect a specific turn and its subagent activity 
  - vault metadata filtering: filter vaults by metadata when listing them 

- beta features we're working on: contact us to try them out
  - memory: agents will be able to remember stuff and search old messages across sessions
  - decisions api: give agents access to the decisions api, for faster performance on tasks that benefit from filtering, classification etc
  - budget control: give the agent a max dollar budget to work within
  - env pooling; we create a pool of vanilla containers,…

items.title: Mistral expands Studio with managed agents, workflows and apps
facts: Today, we’re expanding Studio with managed agents and apps, alongside new capabilities for workflows, enterprise context, agent observability and evaluations.
In Studio, developers can now build agents that carry out complex, multi-step tasks.
Developers can equip them with skills that capture the team’s procedures, sandboxes where they can run code, and subagents to delegate parts of a task.

x_posts.author: @iveyzen
x_posts.text:
Mistral has expanded Studio, its enterprise platform for building AI agents, workflows and apps. Managed agents can use code sandboxes, delegate work to subagents and follow team procedures while Studio handles the runtime.

Workflows define which steps follow rules, where an agent reasons and where a person approves. Mistral says the update adds event triggers from enterprise systems, and interrupted runs can resume.

The platform supports cloud and on-premises deployment options. Managed agents and workflows are in public preview; teams should check which deployment and data-storage arrangements apply to their setup, and test their own edge cases.

https://mistral.ai/news/build-with-studio/

x_posts.author: @ChristopheLams
x_posts.text:
4/ Mistral Studio adds Managed Agents you can deploy in cloud, VPC, or on-prem. Skills, sandboxes, subagents, approval hooks; describe workflows in plain language via Vibe.

Why it matters: enterprise agents with sovereignty baked in.

https://mistral.ai/news/build-with-studio/

items.title: Discussions highlight process changes needed for AI coding agents
facts: Most engineering teams added AI coding agents and changed nothing else
Same review process Same people reviewing Same idea of who owns the code
The tools landed. The process did not

x_posts.author: @madsonmac
x_posts.text:
Most engineering teams added AI coding agents and changed nothing else

Same review process

Same people reviewing

Same idea of who owns the code

I see this almost every time I look at a team

The tools landed. The process did not

So now the output is different every time

Review becomes the bottleneck

Nobody is sure who owns the code the agent wrote

And the risk just goes up quietly

Before you add another agent, answer two questions

Who reviews what it writes

Who owns it after it ships
